text: Here is an answer that would lose the marks, on the card. Our framing: describe the role of ATP in mitosis. Read this answer. Look at the words DNA replication here, and cytokinesis here. It is easy to see why they get written: both processes use energy, and both belong to the cycle you have just followed round the wheel. But the question asks about mitosis, the division of the nucleus, and on the wheel those two sit outside the M arc: replication in the S phase, cytokinesis in the C arc. For this two-mark question the mark scheme says to ignore references to replication or cytokinesis. That is not a claim that ATP goes unused there; it means neither point on this card gains credit. So answer inside the M arc. In place: ATP supplies energy for spindle formation and for movement of daughter chromosomes to opposite poles.
